### Observed differences

- In the later window, activity A02 appears in about 34% of traces (up from 8%) and occurs early (mean position 0.35 vs 0.51); it now precedes A19, A20, A21, A22, A23, A25, A29 and A30 in about 30% of traces, whereas before it rarely co-occurred with them (cooccurrence 8%). [OCC001, POS001, REL002, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL001, REL003]

- Activities A19, A21 and A24 moved from late (mean position about 0.69) to early (about 0.35–0.37). [POS002, POS004, POS007]

- Activities A20, A22 and A23 moved from early (about 0.39) to late (about 0.64). [POS003, POS005, POS006]

- The order between these two groups reversed: before, A20/A22/A23/A25 preceded A19/A21/A24; after, A19/A21/A24 precede A20/A22/A23/A25. For example, A20 before A19 in 31% of traces before, after A19 before A20 in 44% of traces. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030]

- Successor changes: A19, A21 and A24 now go to A25 (about 95–100%) instead of A30 (about 97% before); A20, A22 and A23 now go to A30 (about 32–34%) instead of A25 (about 30–39% before). [DIR002, DIR004, DIR007, DIR003, DIR005, DIR006]

- A02 now leads to A19, A21 and A24 (37%, 24%, 27% of its outgoing transitions) instead of a spread over many activities. [DIR001]

- A40 now leads to A02, A19, A21 and A24 (31%, 29%, 20%, 18%) instead of A20, A22 and A23. [DIR009]

- A41 mean occurrences per trace increased from 1.51 to 1.77 (recurrence support 0.325 to 0.4). [OCC002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a reordering of the process: activities A19, A21 and A24 now occur earlier in the trace, while A20, A22, A23 and A25 occur later, reversing their previous order. A02 appears as a new early activity, and A30 and A25 swap roles as successors of these groups. The volume of evidence (58 items vs 0.75 expected by chance) and the consistency across occurrence, position, order and successor indicators make this a strong hypothesis. A competing explanation of random sampling variation is unlikely given the magnitude and coherence of the changes.

Other differences: A41 shows a modest increase in repetitions per trace. A40's outgoing transitions shifted from A20/A22/A23 to A02/A19/A21/A24. These are consistent with the reordering but not part of the main hypothesis.
